summary.title: Complete Pi Model Doctor audit fixes and final ownership review
summary.what: Completed the V3 audit remediation across the root Pi package: full refresh/check reporting, versioned catalog/provider/policy caches, provider-specific reasoning and cache compatibility mappings, safe headless authorization, migration and sync lifecycles, third-party channel handling, transport and header ownership, atomic backup/rollback behavior, conditional HTTP refresh hardening, documentation, and an expanded integration/regression suite. The final review additionally corrected model-level api/input findings so user-deleted managed fields remain explicitly user-owned and non-repairable.
summary.why: Bring Pi Model Doctor from a usable core implementation to the acceptance and safety boundaries defined by the V3 implementation plan while preserving existing models.json data, avoiding secret exposure, and making all mutation and cache behavior testable and recoverable.

decisions.point: Ownership semantics for deleted managed fields
decisions.chose: Treat deletion of a previously snapshotted managed field as a user-owned edit and report it as non-repairable.
decisions.rationale: Automatic restoration would override an explicit user action and violate the managedValues conflict boundary.

decisions.chose: Only the explicit Done choice completes selection; a falsy UI selection cancels the entire proposal with not-persisted status.
decisions.rationale: Cancellation at any step must not apply an accidentally partial selection.

decisions.chose: Preserve safe prior ETag/Last-Modified values when a 200 response omits replacements, and reject credential-like or newline-bearing validators before cache writes.
decisions.rationale: This retains conditional refresh efficiency without allowing unsafe response metadata into local cache files.

decisions.chose: Perform implementation and final code review directly in the main session without subagents.
decisions.rationale: This preserves the user's explicit execution constraint.

rejected.alternative: Silently restore absent fields whenever catalog metadata provides a value.
rejected.reason: It would erase user-owned deletions and make check/fix ownership reporting inconsistent.

rejected.alternative: Treat a canceled sync selection as equivalent to Done.
rejected.reason: It could persist a partial model set that the user did not authorize.

rejected.alternative: Drop prior conditional validators whenever a successful response omits them.
rejected.reason: It unnecessarily disables later conditional requests and weakens cache behavior.

acknowledged_constraints.note: All implementation, testing, documentation, and code review work was performed in the main session.

review_notes: Final main-session code review found and fixed one ownership-reporting inconsistency for deleted model api/input fields.
Validation passed after the review fix: npm run typecheck, npm test (78/78), npm pack --dry-run --json, and git diff --check.

The older proposed intent int_0c30b9ab is the historical base implementation; its overlap with this follow-up audit intent is expected and not a semantic conflict.

subsystems: migration, sync, rollback, and backup lifecycle
architectural_claims: The published root Pi package separates slash-command authorization/UI from domain proposal and persistence logic.
All models.json mutations use proposal fingerprints, ownership snapshots, timestamped backups, atomic replacement, and persisted read-back verification.
models.dev data is normalized into separate versioned model, provider, and policy caches with schema, permission, secret, and validator checks.
Reasoning and prompt/context/KV cache behavior is resolved through normalized policies and provider adapters, with unsupported Pi runtime behavior represented as compat metadata or warnings.
Third-party channel transport fields remain channel-owned while models.dev metadata may be used only as explicit advisory model metadata.
behavioral_changes: refresh performs a non-mutating configuration check and reports catalog status, findings, and repairable changes.
Headless mutations require --yes and every dry-run path avoids configuration, backup, and cache writes.
migrate, sync, cleanup-backups, and rollback provide explicit safe lifecycle operations.
Interactive sync cancellation at any selection step is not-persisted.
Deleted managed provider and model identity/capability fields are treated as user-owned conflicts rather than silently restored.
Conditional refresh retains safe prior validators when replacements are absent and rejects unsafe response validators.
Successful mutations report runtime activation status when Pi registry verification is available.

api_changes.signature: ModelDoctor.proposeSync/applySync, proposeMigrate/applyMigrate, rollback and full refresh/check lifecycle methods
PI_MODEL_DOCTOR_DIR, PI_MODEL_DOCTOR_MODELS_PATH, PI_MODEL_DOCTOR_MODELS_DEV_URL, refresh interval/jitter and trusted endpoint controls

data_model_changes.name: PolicyCatalog and provider capability cache
data_model_changes.migration_notes: Invalid or incompatible cache schemas are ignored and safely regenerated.

security_implications: Mutations require explicit non-interactive authorization and dry-run takes precedence over --yes.
API keys, authorization headers, OAuth fields, error messages, findings, and plans are redacted or rejected before output/cache persistence.
Catalog endpoints and response bodies are bounded and validated against credential, private-host, unsafe-header, and size/timeout conditions.
Cache directories and files use restrictive permissions and serialized atomic writes.
User-owned transport and capability fields are not overwritten after edits or deletions.
migration_notes: Existing models.json files remain backward compatible and require no migration.
Model migration keeps the source by default and removes it only with --remove-source.
Timestamped backups support explicit rollback; backup cleanup remains a separate authorized operation.
